content: where can i call people and ask them to buy shares in my name

Yes, sir—but only through a **SEBI-registered stockbroker** or their official dealing desk, not an unknown person who promises to buy shares for you.

**Safe process in India:**
1. Open and verify a **demat and trading account** with a SEBI-registered broker.
2. Call the broker using the phone number on its official website or app.
3. Give a specific order: company/ticker, buy or sell, quantity, and market or limit price.
4. Confirm the order and request the **order ID and contract note**.
5. Check that the trade appears in your own demat/trading account.

A broker may execute orders on your behalf, but you should not hand over your login password, OTP, PIN, or unrestricted control of your demat account. Verify the intermediary through SEBI’s registered-intermediary database. ([investor.sebi.gov.in](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/Brokers.html?utm_source=openai))

For general investor assistance, SEBI’s helpline is **1800-266-7575** or **1800-22-7575**, available Monday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–6 p.m. except declared Maharashtra public holidays. ([investor.sebi.gov.in](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/Investor-support.html?utm_source=openai))

You can also tell me your country and whether you already have a broker account, and I’ll explain the safest next step.
india, mumbaii

Understood, sir—**Mumbai, India**.

Your safest choices are:

- Visit the Mumbai office of a **SEBI-registered stockbroker**.
- Call the broker’s **official dealing desk** and ask them to execute orders from your own trading account.
- Use the broker’s official mobile app or website yourself.

Before dealing with anyone, verify the broker on SEBI’s official **Registered Stock Brokers** list; it includes location and registration details. ([sebi.gov.in](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/other/OtherAction.do?doRecognisedFpi=yes&intmId=30&utm_source=openai))

You can say:

> “I have a trading and demat account with your firm. Please help me place a buy order. I will confirm the stock, quantity, and price.”

Never give anyone your **OTP, password, PIN, or full account control**. Deal only with the registered broker—not an individual promising guaranteed returns. SEBI specifically advises investors to deal only with registered intermediaries. ([investor.sebi.gov.in](https://investor.sebi.gov.in/Brokers.html?utm_source=openai))
groww

**Groww is suitable, sir.** It is an online Indian stockbroker, so you can buy shares through the Groww app using your own trading and demat account. Groww supports Indian stocks listed on NSE and BSE. ([resources.groww.in](https://resources.groww.in/web-assets/media-library/2025/9/UDRHP%20-%201.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To get help, use the **Help & Support** section inside the Groww app. Groww’s official support page also lists customer care at **+91 9108800000**; verify the number in the app before calling, and never share your password, PIN, OTP, or screen access. ([groww.in](https://groww.in/help/my-account/searchable/how-to-call-groww-customer-care?utm_source=openai))

**Basic steps:**
1. Open Groww and search for the company.
2. Tap **Buy**.
3. Select **quantity** and **Market** or **Limit** order.
4. Review the details carefully.
5. Place the order yourself.

During Indian market hours—generally **9:15 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays**—orders are sent to the exchange; after hours, they are held for the next market opening. ([groww.in](https://groww.in/help/stocks/order/when-will-my-order-be-placed?utm_source=openai))
